promises.quote: In 2015/16, the trust carried out a significant recruitment campaign and educated 350 whole time equivalent frontline posts.
promises.summary: Trust will recruit 350 frontline staff to improve ambulance resources.

promises.quote: EMAS has taken the CQC findings seriously and value the additional support from other NHS organisations following the CQC Quality Summit. With their input EMAS can progress areas that cannot be fixed quickly, or that are not within EMAS' immediate control.
promises.summary: EMAS will implement outcomes of independent strategic demand, capacity and price review to meet demand

concerns.quote: I remain very concerned about resource issues for this ambulance service. I raised similar concerns in a Prevention of Future Deaths Report in the case of MG, dated 11 May 2016.
I consider that there is a risk of future deaths as set out above unless an urgent review of resources is undertaken.
Consideration should be given to strategies to improve handover times at hospitals.

concerns.quote: Triaging by '111' and EMAS call handling systems, including in relation to sepsis. In the present case, Mrs Gudgeon had collapsed, passed out, been confused and had been vomiting. These are signs of central nervous system/neurological problems but were not regarded as urgent. Despite EMAS being told that Mrs Gudgeon may have a urinary tract infection, no escalation occurred.

It was suggested in evidence that if the same facts are inputted into the '999' AMPDS triaging system they are likely to allocate a higher priority to the call than the '111' Pathway triaging system would.
concerns.hazard: Inconsistent priority allocation across triage systems

concerns.quote: The shortage of double crewed ambulances and fast response vehicles in the Northampton Division.

The effectiveness of the EMAS Capacity Management & Escalation Plan (CMP) including, inter alia, the fact that:‐ a) CMP status 1 - 3 does not trigger the deployment of additional 2 vehicular resources. b) CMP 4 is only triggered when 200 calls are holding (this was previously 150) - this is a high threshold. c) A Technical Commander can overrule a CMP status e.g. even if 200 calls are holding (CMP 4), this can simply be downgraded to CMP 3 by the Technical Commander
concerns.hazard: Capacity Management Plan thresholds and overrides delay response

links.explanation: Both reports highlight insufficient ambulance resources as a risk to patient safety. The later report narrows the concern to a shortage of double‑crewed ambulances and fast response vehicles in a specific division.
